links.outcome: Physician performance with AI assistance versus conventional resources; omission of AI-generated recommendations
links.effect: In a randomized study of 101 physicians, AI assistance improved performance compared to conventional resources, but AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.
links.quote: In a randomized study of 101 U.S.-licensed generalist physicians, AI assistance improved physician performance compared to conventional resources.

links.outcome: Frequency and severity of harmful errors, especially omissions, in LLM consultation recommendations
links.effect: Direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.
links.quote: Across 20 notable LLMs and 4 widely used retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) clinical AI tools, direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.

links.outcome: Whether medical knowledge benchmark performance predicts clinical safety of deployed AI tools
links.effect: Despite strong performance on medical knowledge benchmarks, widely used AI tools can produce consultation advice with potential for severe harm.
links.quote: Collectively, these results show that despite strong performance on medical knowledge benchmarks, widely used AI tools can produce medical consultation advice with the potential for severe harm, and highlight the need for explicit measurement of clinical safety.

links.outcome: Physician uptake of valuable AI recommendations in AI-assisted consultation
links.effect: AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI-generated recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.
links.quote: However, AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI-generated recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.
